newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: ASIAN EXOTICS-Thai interbank rate surges,baht weak.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN EXOTICS-Thai interbank rate surges,baht weak.

text.p: * Thai overnight interbank rate surges to new six-month high on heavy fund demand for Lunar New Year and central bank's reserve requirement. Baht hit by continued outflows of funds, strong dollar.
* Indonesian rupiah stable in slow trade as market prepares for long weekend.
* Money markets in Malaysia and Singapore closed for Chinese and Moslem new years. Trading to resume on February 11.
Thai asset markets remained under pressure on Friday as investors pulled out of the baht due to continuing poor sentiment and the dollar's strong tone.

The baht was quoted at 25.980-25.985 to the dollar at 0400 GMT against 25.985-25.995 late on Thursday. The Bank of Thailand (BOT) fixed the baht/dollar mid-rate at 25.92, the lowest level in over five years, against 25.90 on Thursday.
Bangkok forex dealers said trade was very slow with both Singapore and Hong Kong players out for the Chinese New Year holiday.

The overnight interbank rate was quoted at 25.00-26.00 percent early, the highest level since July 31, 1996, as most commercial banks were short of funds. The interbank rate was at 20.00-22.00 percent late on Thursday.
Dealers attributed the high demand for funds this week to the seasonal high spending for the Lunar New Year and the central bank's reserve deadline which is due on Friday.
"The close of Singapore and Hong Kong markets today also reduced foreign funds into the market," said a foreign bank dealer.
A senior BOT official said on Friday the central bank was monitoring the money market and that the current tight liquidity situation was not worrisome.

"We monitor the market closely and have all necessary mechanisms to fine tune the market," Nongnart Sondisuwan, deputy director of Financial Institutions Supervision and Development Department told Reuters.
"There is no reason to worry about the situation in the money market," she said.
The central bank had limited its fund injection into the money market because it did not want to encourage speculative forex activities among commercial banks, she said.
In Indonesia, the rupiah was relatively steady in slow trade as most players focused on the short-term money and swap markets, dealers said.
A local bank dealer in Jakarta said spreads were wide due to the thin market with public holidays in Singapore and Hong Kong.
In Jakarta many operators had already left to celebrate the Lunar New Year and the Moslem Eid al-Fitr holiday.
The foreign exchange market will be closed for Eid al-Fitr on February 10 and 11 inclusive, while the stock market will be closed from February 7 to 11 inclusive.
The local bank dealer said foreign banks were seen taking up short-term swaps to meet the central bank's rules on net-open positions, keeping the money market volatile.
The central bank raised its intervention band by one point to 2,375/2,567 and the conversion band to 2,375/2,423 on Thursday, the third depreciation this week.
-- Mantik Kusjanto in Jakarta (62-21-384-6364), Anuchit Nguyen in Bangkok (662) 652-0642 and Sonali Desai in Singapore (65-8703090)
